The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924501;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924501;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924501;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #316e22;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #316e22;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #316e22;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3a2b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3a2b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #316e22;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #316e22;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #316e22;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3353c1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #316e22;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #316e22;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #316e22;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6348af;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3a2b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3a2b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6348af;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6348af;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #316e22;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #316e22;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #316e22;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #80399f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #80399f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #316e22;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #316e22;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #316e22;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006787;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006787;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006787;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3b76;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8c3b76;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3b76;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924501;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924501;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924501;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596500;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #596500;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596500;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0062a3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3b76;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3b76;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3b76;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3a2b;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3a2b;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #246d4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3353c1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #924501;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #924501;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #924501;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6348af;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6348af;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6348af;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9e2e51;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2e51;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d14;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d14;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3353c1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3353c1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
